# Notefox

> Notefox is a free, open-source browser extension that lets you take notes on any website.

Notefox allows users to create, manage, and sync notes directly linked to web pages. Notes are stored locally in the browser and can optionally be synced across devices with end-to-end encryption via a free account. The extension is available for Firefox, Google Chrome, and Microsoft Edge.

## Key facts

- Type: Browser extension (WebExtension)
- Price: Free and open-source (GPL-3.0)
- Author: Saverio Morelli
- Browsers: Firefox, Chrome, Edge
- Languages: English, Italian, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Portuguese (BR), Portuguese (PT), Polish, Chinese (Simplified), Japanese, Arabic, Dutch
- Sync: Optional, end-to-end encrypted (AES-256), revision-based conflict detection
- Account system: Email-based with OTP verification
- Data stored: Notes are stored locally in the browser; synced data is encrypted at rest on the server

## Features

- Take notes on any website with a browser popup
- Notes are linked to the page URL
- Rich text formatting
- Search through all notes
- Optional cloud sync across devices
- End-to-end encryption for synced data
- Multi-browser support
- Open-source codebase on GitHub
- No ads, no tracking

## API

The Notefox REST API (v2) is available at `https://notefox.eu/api/v2`. It powers account management, authentication (with optional OTP), and encrypted data sync. All user data is encrypted at rest using AES-256-CBC with a per-user DEK (Data Encryption Key). The API uses revision-based conflict detection for sync operations. Full documentation is at https://www.notefox.eu/alpha/docs/.

## Technical architecture

- Server-side encryption: password → PBKDF2 → KEK → wraps DEK → encrypts all user data
- The server never stores plaintext email (SHA-512 hash only) or plaintext passwords
- Sync uses revision numbers for conflict detection
- Rate limiting is per-account, not per-service
- Sessions use 64-character hex login-id and token pairs
